state.case_summary:
A 40-year-old man presented with a painful nodule on the lower part of his right leg. He reported that the lesion had been stable in size and painless for 4 years but had enlarged and become tender over the past 6 months. There was no history of trauma or personal or family history of malignancy.

On examination, an irregular, firm, erythematous, mobile, tender mass measuring 3.5 × 2.3 × 1.7 cm was noted just above the lateral malleolus of the right leg. No popliteal or inguinal lymphadenopathy was present, and there were no other suspicious cutaneous lesions. Routine blood tests, including complete blood count, fasting blood sugar, liver and renal function tests, were within normal limits. Tests for hepatitis B surface antigen and HIV were negative.

The patient underwent a local excision. Grossly, there was a lobulated, tan-gray, firm mass partly covered by skin, measuring 3.5 × 2.3 × 1.7 cm. On light microscopy, the dermal tumor extended into the superficial subcutis and was composed of nests and fascicles of spindle-shaped to epithelioid cells with pale eosinophilic cytoplasm, vesicular nuclei, and prominent nucleoli within a collagenous stroma. Mitotic figures, including atypical forms, measured 7–8 per 10 high-power fields. There was no intracytoplasmic melanin pigment, and the overlying epidermis showed no increase in basal melanocytes, junctional activity, or pagetoid spread.

Immunohistochemical staining showed strong positivity for vimentin and focal positivity for Melan-A and HMB-45. The tumor cells were negative for S-100 protein, pancytokeratin, epithelial membrane antigen, and CD31.
